h1: The 6 Best FlexiSpot Standing Desk Converters of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six FlexiSpot standing desk converters, electric and gas-spring, from 36 to 42 inches, compared on width, lift type and price.
summary: The FlexiSpot 36 inch electric converter is our best overall pick, since it is the cheapest motorized option. The 42 inch electric gives the most room with a motor, the 40 inch electric sits between, and the gas-spring models are the quiet-budget alternative.
intro: The surprise in FlexiSpot's converter line is how little separates electric and manual models on price. A 36 inch electric converter lands in the same tier as manual ones, so buying a gas-spring riser by default can mean skipping a motor you could have afforded.
We ranked six FlexiSpot models on platform width, lift type and price tier. Two others were left out, one with no listed price and one with a thin spec line, and every claim comes from the listings.

products.name: FLEXISPOT 36 Inch Electric Standing Desk Converter, Motorized Sit to Stand Riser
products.verdict: An electric lift with a 36 inch platform at the lower price tier.
products.description:
This FlexiSpot has a 36 inch platform and electric lift, priced $100-200.

It wins because it brings a motor into the cheaper bucket, where the gas-spring models also sit. The tradeoff versus the 42 inch electric is less surface, not fewer features.

Buy it if you want push-button height changes on a standard desk. It needs a power outlet nearby.
products.idealFor: Standard desks that need a motor on a budget.

products.name: FLEXISPOT 42 Inch Electric Motor Desk Converter, Height Adjustable Motorized
products.verdict: The widest electric FlexiSpot here, in the $200-500 tier.
products.description:
The 42 inch electric model has a motorized lift and a 42 inch platform, priced $200-500.

It places second because the same motor in the 36 inch model costs a tier less. The extra price buys six inches of surface.

Choose it for a dual-screen or multi-device setup. If 36 inches covers you, save the money.

products.name: FLEXISPOT 40 Inch Electric Standing Desk Converter, Height Adjustable Riser
products.verdict: A 40 inch electric converter between the 36 and 42.
products.description:
The 40 inch electric riser has a 40 inch platform and an electric lift. Its price tier is $200-500.

It ranks third because it shares the 42 inch model's price tier with less width. The only reason to choose it is a desk that cannot take 42 inches.

Pick it for a desk that sits between sizes. Otherwise go smaller for savings or larger for room.

products.name: FLEXISPOT Standing Desk Converter 42 Inch, Extra Large Ergonomic Height Adjustable
products.verdict: A 42 inch gas-spring riser at the lower price tier.
products.description:
This FlexiSpot has a 42 inch platform and a manual gas-spring lift, priced $100-200.

It ranks fourth because it gives the 42 inch width without the motor price. The tradeoff is lifting it by hand against the gas spring.

Choose it for a wide desk when you stand now and then. If you switch often, take the electric 36 inch instead.

products.name: FLEXISPOT Standing Desk Converter 40 Inch Large Desk Riser, Spacious
products.verdict: A 40 inch gas-spring riser in the cheaper tier.
products.description:
The 40 inch riser has a manual gas-spring lift and a 40 inch platform, priced $100-200.

It lands fifth because the 42 inch manual model offers more width in the same tier. Its case is for desks where two inches matters.

Buy it for a mid-width desk and low cost. Expect to raise it by hand.

products.name: FLEXISPOT Standing Desk Converter 36 Inch Desk Riser, Height Adjustable
products.verdict: A 36 inch gas-spring riser in the same tier as the electric 36.
products.description:
The 36 inch manual riser uses a gas-spring lift and costs $100-200.

It finishes last because the 36 inch electric model sits in the same tier with a motor. That makes this one hard to justify unless you want no power cord.

Buy it if you want a cordless setup. Otherwise the electric version above is the better deal.

whatMatters.detail: Electric lifts move at a button press, while gas-spring lifts rise by hand against a spring. It matters if you change position often. The listing says electric or gas-spring.
Width sets how much you can fit. 36 inches suits a laptop and a monitor, while 42 inches suits more. Compare the inch figure to your desk.
Tiers here run from $100-200 to $200-500. Because a 36 inch electric costs as little as manual ones, check before paying more. Read the bucket along with the lift type.
Electric models need an outlet near the desk, manual ones do not. This matters for desks far from a socket. Check where your cable can run.
A converter takes up desk depth too. Measure your desk before choosing. The listing gives the platform inches but check depth on the product page.
